subject: Region tethering validation & rollback playbook — Acme Payments request
messages:
From: Sara Hoffman <sara.hoffman@acmepay.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: security@acmepay.com
Date: 2028-06-01T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: validation of region tethering and rollback playbook

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our vendor review for Dedicated deployments, our security team needs two things before we can sign off on production onboarding: a concise validation that our tenant will be pinned to the requested US region boundaries (no cross-region replication of tenant data), and an operations rollback playbook that details how Redwood will sanitize tenant data and rollback a pinned deployment in case of misconfiguration or emergency.

Specifically we need: 
- A short matrix that maps tenant logical artifacts (logs, model cache, backups, snapshots) to their physical location and retention behavior.
- A documented rollback playbook with steps, expected RTO/RPO and verification checks.
- Evidence or a timeline showing how a tenant wipe is performed and how long snapshots/replicas persist before permanent deletion.

We appreciate sample artifacts or redacted evidence; we can sign an NDA if required for more detailed traces. Can you provide the matrix and playbook, and a brief note confirming your in-region isolation mechanisms? Also please advise if there are any scenarios where data might leave the pinned region.

Thanks,
Sara Hoffman
Head of Security, Acme Payments
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sara Hoffman <sara.hoffman@acmepay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-01T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: validation of region tethering and rollback playbook

Sara —

Thanks for the clear list. We can provide everything you asked for. I attached an initial region-to-artifact matrix (region_tethering_matrix.csv) that maps the high-level artifact classes to physical location and retention defaults. It's redacted for public transmission; we can provide the full export under NDA.

Quick notes:
- Dedicated tenants are pinned to a region by deployment binding; persistent volumes, KV stores for cache, and snapshot storage are provisioned in-region by default.
- Backups are only replicated cross-region if a customer explicitly enables cross-region DR or the account is on a cross-region Dedicated plan; otherwise we do not replicate.
- We keep a 7-day snapshot retention default for ephemeral caches and a separately-configurable retention for backups (customer-controlled).

Marissa (CC'd) will share the rollback playbook and a sanitized wipe checklist. Could we schedule a 30-min call tomorrow to walk Acme through the playbook and acceptance criteria? I can host.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Director, Platform Security & Operations
Redwood Inference

Hi Sara / team —

Attaching our current rollback playbook (rollback_playbook_v2.pdf). High level overview below and quick answers to the questions in your email: 

High-level rollback playbook summary:
- Triggering events: mis-pin detected, unauthorized cross-region replication, confirmed leakage, or customer request.
- Immediate actions (T0–T15): isolate tenant routing (disable external ingress), snapshot current volumes (read-only), pause automated replication jobs.
- Recovery/rollback (T15–T120): failover to a validated in-region standby (if available) or redeploy a fresh pinned instance from in-region snapshot.
- Sanitization/wipe (T120–T720): run tenant-scoped purge that removes tenant blobs, metadata indexes, and revokes keys. Follow with verification scans and snapshot expiry enforcement.
- Verification: cryptographic snapshot manifests and deletion receipts stored in audit logs; we can provide redacted receipts under NDA.

Retention & snapshot behavior:
- Snapshot retention is configurable per-tenant. Default backup retention is 30 days; ephemeral caches default to 7 days.
- Snapshots are stored encrypted at rest with per-tenant keys, and we retain snapshot manifests in our audit store for 90 days for forensic purposes.

Edge cases where data can leave the pinned region:
- Scheduled cross-region DR (explicit customer opt-in only).
- Customer-initiated export (S3/HTTP) or manual admin action.

Next steps:
1) I've attached rollback_playbook_v2.pdf and included a sanitized checklist we typically share with customers.
2) Dev will provide a short run of the actual wipe steps and command examples for your ops team.
3) Jonas, can you confirm whether Acme needs an SLA exception or dedicated replication controls?

Marissa Cole
Senior Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: validation of region tethering and rollback playbook

Sara —

Following up with the technical sequence for a tenant-scoped sanitization and the verification checks we run. Attaching the checklist (sanitization_checklist.xlsx). Below is a condensed example of the steps we run in a coordinated operation: 

1) Disable ingress & pause writers (API gateway rules) — confirmation via routing table snapshot.
2) Snapshot volumes (read-only) and export manifests to audit store.
3) Run tenant-scoped purge: delete objects by tenant-id prefix from object store and drop tenant-specific indices from DB shard.
4) Rotate KMS keys associated with tenant caches to prevent access to older caches.
5) Trigger background GC and enforce snapshot expiry policy (we set snapshot-delete TTL to 0 for immediate purge when requested).
6) Post-wipe verification: run checksum scans and index-absence checks; produce deletion receipts.

A few operational notes:
- Immediate purge is best-effort for object stores; underlying cloud provider soft-delete windows can introduce short-lived retention — we surface this to customers and include time-to-permanent-delete in the playbook.
- For Dedicated deployments, we can schedule a controlled snapshot expiry that enforces an accelerated deletion window if required in the contract.

Attachments include the checklist and an obfuscated example of the deletion receipt format. Happy to walk your engineers through command samples.

—Dev Patel
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
Attachments: sanitization_checklist.xlsx (XLSX, 26KB)

Sara —

Bringing this across the finish line. Attached are the three artifacts we've discussed: region_tethering_matrix.csv, rollback_playbook_v2.pdf, sanitization_checklist.xlsx. Summary of guarantees and acceptance criteria for Acme to review: 

- Region pinning: Tenant deployment bindings ensure all persistent volumes, snapshots and runtime KV caches remain in the pinned US region unless cross-region DR is explicitly enabled.
- No implicit cross-region replication: We do not replicate tenant artifacts across regions by default. Any replication requires account-level opt-in.
- Wipe verification: We provide deletion receipts and an audit-log manifest (redacted) after purge operations. If you require irrevocable immediate deletion SLAs beyond our standard contract, we'll need to add a clause to the Dedicated agreement that specifies accelerated snapshot expiry and provider-side retention windows.

Proposed next steps: 
1) Book a 30-min technical walkthrough Thursday 2028-06-03 09:00 PT (I will send a calendar invite).
2) If Acme needs deeper artifacts (full manifests or cryptographic receipts) we can share them under an NDA.
3) If you want an accelerated deletion SLA, Marissa will follow up with contract language and a pricing note.

Please confirm the time or propose alternatives. If this looks good, we can close the review and move Acme to Dedicated onboarding.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Director, Platform Security & Operations
Redwood Inference
